questions.q: What level is the UART line at when idle for a regular, uninverted signal?
questions.explain: Idle is logical one, the high level. The start bit pulls the line down to zero.

options: A protocol on top of I2C with a receiver address
questions.explain: SBUS: 100 kbaud, 8 bits, even parity, 2 stop bits; the inverted signal is the protocol standard, not an exception.

questions.q: Why does CRSF work on any UART of any board?
options: It's slow and doesn't need a buffer
questions.explain: CRSF is standard 8N1 without inversion, full duplex on two wires.

options: SBUS over a CRSF wire without parity
questions.explain: The data is the same, the signal is flipped back — to work around the missing inverter on F4.

questions.q: CRSF: channels work, no telemetry on the radio. What do you check?
options: The receiver antenna and the VTX channel
The FC TX → RX wire and halfduplex
questions.explain: Telemetry goes over the return wire. Without it, or in half-duplex, there's none.

questions.q: What is the spec CRSF speed for onboard full duplex?
questions.explain: The TBS spec: 416666 baud 8N1, with the option to negotiate a higher speed.

questions.q: What does the CRC8 in a CRSF frame cover?
questions.explain: Type and payload, without sync and length; polynomial 0xD5 — per the TBS spec.

questions.q: An SBUS receiver is connected to the RX of a free UART on an F4 board without a separate inverter. No signal. Why?
questions.fragment:
serial 2 64 115200 57600 0 115200
set serialrx_provider = SBUS
set serialrx_inverted = OFF
options: SBUS is inverted, and the F4 UART can't invert by itself — you need an input with an inverter
SBUS only works on UART1 because it requires hardware DMA
The speed in the serial command must be 100000, otherwise Betaflight won't open the port
SBUS requires serialrx_inverted = ON on any board, and F4 supports it
questions.explain: On F4 inversion is done by an external circuit; F7/H7 can invert the UART in software.
